note: Item codes Home1..Home6 are the .sav column names W2_HomeN with the W2_ wave prefix stripped by data/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_build.py (crosswalk key homespace; waves=[2]; code IS the source column name after prefix strip, no positional step, no recode or reverse-coding). The .sav variable labels read "To what extent do the following statements about the amount of private space in someone's home apply to you?\nPlease simply skip statements that do not apply to you (e.g. if you don't have children or live alone) - <statement>"; the shared stem plus skip instruction went to instructions (the embedded newline replaced by a space) and the statement to item_text, 6/6 identical to the Q293 grid rows in the W2 questionnaire and to the numbered list in measures information 2.2.3.2, same order. option_text = the .sav value labels 1=Strongly disagree, 2=Disagree, 3=Somewhat disagree, 4=Neither agree nor disagree, 5=Somewhat agree, 6=Agree, 7=Strongly agree, identical for all 6 items and matching the questionnaire column headers. The .sav also carries user-missing -99 (skipped), which the build drops; measures information says a not-applicable option was included, but neither the questionnaire grid nor the .sav has an N/A code beyond the skip instruction and -99. Cross-check (not required for data_labels): .sav per-item x resp counts match the live table cell-for-cell, 42/42 (e.g. Home1 29/26/39/95/181/315/594, Home2 554/297/125/125/112/53/50); live table is wave 2 only, 7335 rows, 1379 ids. Data caveat: the two child items pile up at the midpoint -- Home3 420/1051 and Home4 427/1026 at 4=Neither, against 83-125 for the other four items. Cross-tab against W2_Children_household: of Home3's 1051 responses only 338 come from respondents reporting >=1 child in the household; 302 of its 420 midpoint responses come from respondents reporting 0 children (and 95 from respondents coded lives-alone/missing), so many non-parents answered neutral instead of skipping as instructed (Home4 similar: 334 of 1026 responses from respondents with children; 304 of its 427 midpoints from 0-children respondents, 93 from lives-alone/missing). Study-authored items (measures information cites no source instrument for 2.2.3.2); no rights-holder restriction beyond the deposit's CC BY 4.0. English administration.
public_note: For the two child items (Home3, Home4) roughly 40% of responses sit at the 4 = Neither agree nor disagree midpoint, and most of those come from respondents who reported no children in the household, so the midpoint there largely reflects not-applicable answers rather than neutral agreement.
